content:
Hi all — alongside the three-gap PR, I've formalized Farey sequences as an object plus the underlying mediant / Stern–Brocot theory, which I couldn't find in Mathlib.

Highlights (all in Mathlib/NumberTheory/Farey/Basic.lean):

  • Farey.farey n : Finset ℚ — the Farey sequence F n (reduced rationals in [0,1], denominator ≤ n), with Farey.mem_farey.
  • Farey.card_farey — the length |F n| = 1 + ∑_{k=1}^n φ(k).
  • Farey.neighbour_unimodular — the neighbour theorem (Hardy–Wright Thm 28): consecutive terms a/b < c/d satisfy b·c − a·d = 1; restated on the object as Farey.unimodular_of_consecutive.
  • the mediant core: Unimodular.isCoprime_mediant, the denominator bound Unimodular.den_ge_of_strictBetween (mediant is the unique simplest fraction strictly between neighbours), the Stern–Brocot step isFareyChain_insert_mediant, and the gap formula Unimodular.rat_sub : c/d − a/b = 1/(b·d).

All sorry-free; #print axioms on each main result reports only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Draft PR: #40246.

These are classical results (Hardy–Wright Ch. III; Graham–Knuth–Patashnik §4.5) — the value is reusable infrastructure, not new mathematics. Mathlib has the continued-fraction convergent determinant identity and Legendre's theorem, but those concern the convergents of a single real, a different object from F n.

Questions: (1) would Mathlib want this, and is anyone already on it? (2) placement OK at NumberTheory/Farey/?

Disclosure: developed with AI assistance; fully machine-checked and axiom-audited as above.
